transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-08 15:00 PDT | Duration 52m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood CS), Danielle Moore (Brookside Head Eng), Miguel Santos (CTO), Ravi Patel (Platform Eng), Hannah Lee (Security)

Summary: quick demo of org/project keys and rate-limiting controls, Q&A about security and PoC next steps.

00:00 Alex Chen: hey everybody thanks for joining, uh looks like we have a full room from Brookside, appreciate the time, I'll hand it over to Priya to walk through the console and the API flows for org and project keys

00:18 Priya Kapoor: cool thanks Alex, um so high level we'll show two things — how you can mint org level keys and project scoped keys, then how you attach rate limit policies and quotas to those keys; we'll also show what happens in high load and how the runtime degrades or falls back to a cheaper model variant, and finally the optimize suggestions for batching. quick question before we start, is there any particular throughput or token per second numbers you care about?

00:39 Miguel Santos: yeah good question. our triage assistant will see peaks when partner clinics hit morning triage, say 500 rps at peak across multiple endpoints, and some endpoints are heavier tokens like summarization so per-second token limits matter. we also need different limits for internal vs external partners.

01:05 Priya Kapoor: got it. that's exactly the use case for org keys + project keys: you create one org, your company, then create projects for each partner or internal product and mint project-scoped keys. you can attach per-project rate limits — e.g., 1000 rps for internal project, 200 rps for partner A, with quotas per day or month.

01:28 Danielle Moore: when you say rps, is that request-level or token-level? we care about both because costs blow up on token-heavy calls.

01:36 Priya Kapoor: great callout. in Redwood we have two dimensions: token throughput limits and request concurrency/rate. in the console you can set token-per-minute or token-per-second policies, and you can also set request-level rate limits. billing is still per-token for hosted, but quotas are enforced on whichever threshold you hit first.

02:03 Ravi Patel: and these quotas can be overridden per-project? like staging vs prod?

02:07 Priya Kapoor: yes you can set defaults at the org level and override per project. often customers create a prod project with higher quotas and a staging project with tighter caps.

02:20 Alex Chen: i'll jump in on pricing note — we'll send a SKU that shows dedicated vs hosted rates and then examples of how rate limits influence estimated monthly cost based on your traffic profile.

02:32 Priya Kapoor: moving to the console — sorry for the slight lag, the recording tool clipped a bit; so here is the org dashboard, you can see aggregate token usage, per-project breakdown, and an interface to create rate-limit policies. i'm going to create a policy called 'partner-A-strict' — set rps to 200, burst 400 for short spikes, monthly quota 5 million tokens. you can attach this policy to the project's key.

03:05 Miguel Santos: burst 400 — how does that interact with autoscale and Dedicated capacity? what if we hit sustained spikes?

03:12 Priya Kapoor: good Q. if you're on Redwood Dedicated we have reserved GPU pools and autoscaling policies. burst allows short windows above steady rate; sustained spikes will either consume more of the dedicated pool (if you've configured burst capacity) or if you're at the top of capacity we'll trigger configured fallbacks — either queueing, rejecting with a 429, or routing to a lower-cost model variant for best-effort responses. we can show a demo of fallback policies in the PoC.

03:45 Hannah Lee: from security perspective, how are the keys stored, and do you support customer KMS/HSM? also SSO for console access?

03:53 Priya Kapoor: keys are encrypted at rest. for Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM; in hosted we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations. Console access supports SSO via SAML/Okta and fine-grained RBAC roles. the audit logs capture key minting and policy changes — we can share the SOC2 and audit log docs after the call.

04:20 Danielle Moore: that's great. we will need to validate audit trails and make sure external partners can't see internal usage.

04:27 Alex Chen: yep — projects scope visibility. project owners only see their project's metrics unless you grant cross-project permissions.

04:35 Priya Kapoor: back to the API — i'll show curl to create a project key. note that the client can call the standard /v1/ endpoints but the request will be rate limited according to the attached policy. here's an example: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer proj_XXXXX' POST to /v1/chat/completions. you'll get a 429 with a Retry-After header if you exceed the limit. the response body also contains policy_id and remaining_quota fields so callers can gracefully degrade.

05:05 Ravi Patel: can the Retry-After be absolute time and do we get per-route breakdowns?

05:10 Priya Kapoor: Retry-After is seconds relative. we also have headers for token-remaining and requests-remaining. for deeper metrics we push granular traces to the console and you can export logs to your SIEM via syslog or cloud export.

05:28 Miguel Santos: curious about multi-tenant pattern — we want to bill partners separately and show them their usage without exposing other customers. is per-project billing supported?

05:37 Alex Chen: yes, projects are the unit for billing if you want. we can generate per-project invoice lines and export to your accounting system; many customers do per-partner billing by assigning each partner a project and using the project key for calls.

05:52 Priya Kapoor: showing a quick example of creating a policy via API: POST /v1/org/policies with JSON body — forgive the transcription, the body has fields like rate_limit_per_second, burst, monthly_quota_tokens, attach_to_project_id. you can also schedule policies or have dynamic policies using tags.

06:20 Danielle Moore: you mentioned tags and dynamic policies — can we do rules like if route == /summarize then lower token quota?

06:27 Priya Kapoor: yes, route-based rules are supported — we let you create rule chains: match by route or model, then apply different token multipliers or hard caps. that's how customers prevent runaway costs from heavy summarization endpoints.

06:40 Miguel Santos: about performance — do rate limit checks add latency to the request path?

06:45 Priya Kapoor: negligible; the checks are performed at the edge before request enters the heavy runtime. we use distributed counters and local caching to keep latency impact under 1ms in most cases; occasional consistency windows exist but we surface the state in headers.

07:05 Ravi Patel: for the PoC we will want SE to drive a load test from our side and from yours to compare. can Redwood seed a traffic emulator?

07:12 Alex Chen: yes we can run a Redwood-managed load test. next step would be you share your traffic profile (CSV), Priya will spin up a test plan, we'll run both hosted and a dedicated-simulated run to show latency and how rate limits behave under real traffic.

07:30 Priya Kapoor: demoing the Optimize tab now — we give batching and quantization suggestions by workload; for high token routes we recommend continuous batching and a quantized model variant which reduces token cost by ~2x at a small latency delta. you can tie optimize rules to projects so production projects get aggressive optimizations while staging does not.

08:00 Hannah Lee: on data residency, some partner clinics require EU data never leave EU. can we pin certain projects to regions?

08:08 Priya Kapoor: yes regional pinning is supported — projects can be assigned to regions and requests routed accordingly. for Private deployments you can keep everything on-prem. we will add region constraints in the PoC scope doc.

08:22 Danielle Moore: ok this is helpful. a couple of quick objections — if we go with hosted and you have an incident, how quickly can we change policies? and is there automation for emergency blacklists?

08:34 Priya Kapoor: policies can be changed immediately via API and take effect within seconds. we also support emergency kill-switch rules at org level and IP blacklists. plus you can have automatic fallback policies that trigger when error rates exceed thresholds.

08:50 Miguel Santos: last question on pricing sensitivity — can rate limits be enforced by API gateway before billing? basically we want to front our own gateway and still have Redwood meter per-project usage.

09:00 Alex Chen: yes many customers operate a gateway in front. Redwood accepts traffic from your gateway keyed by project key; we will meter the downstream tokens. if you throttle at gateway level you can quilt costs but you'll still get per-project usage in our billing exports.

09:18 Priya Kapoor: wrapping up — recap of next steps: Alex will send pricing and SKU, Priya will share console recording and API examples, Brookside to share traffic profile and compliance questions, we'll schedule PoC kickoff.

09:34 Danielle Moore: sounds good, thanks everyone. we'll aim to get the CSV to Ravi by EOD Monday.

09:40 Miguel Santos: appreciate it, excited to see the PoC numbers.

09:45 Alex Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and docs.
